name: dirperm
description: DIRECTORY WRITE PERMISSION IS ENFORCED, AND THE STICKY BIT WITH IT, asked of the RUNNING SYSTEM the way the bug was reported.  apple/fgx#419: ufs_lookup asked VEXEC of a directory and never VWRITE, so any account could create and delete in any directory it could search -- `echo pwned > /etc/zz' and `rm /etc/motd' both succeeded from the unprivileged account against a drwxr-xr-x /etc owned by root, which put `rm /etc/passwd' and `rm /bin/sh' in reach of anybody with a login.  THESE ARE THE ISSUE'S OWN TWO LINES, typed at a real login rather than reimplemented in a test binary: nothing is added to the volume, so the measurement costs the image nothing and cannot perturb what any other fixture boots.  Four probes whose answers must DIFFER, because a run where every answer agrees cannot tell an enforced machine from an open one: c1 and c2 are a create and a delete in /etc and must FAIL; c3 is a create in /tmp and must SUCCEED, which is the control that says the check did not simply break every create on the system -- /tmp and /var/tmp became 1777 in the same increment and vi, sh and half the suite write there; c4 deletes a ROOT-OWNED file from that sticky /tmp and must FAIL, which is the whole reason 1777 is safe to ship.  THE NEEDLES CANNOT BE TYPED: the shell expands `$status' and the digits appear in nothing on the command line.  THE TWO ERRNOS ARE THEMSELVES AN ASSERTION and not decoration: the /etc refusals are EACCES, printed `Permission denied', because ufs_access answered no to VWRITE; the /tmp one is EPERM, `Operation not permitted', because the directory was writable and the STICKY rule refused it.  A machine that enforced the directory mode and skipped the sticky test would delete root's file and print nothing at all there.  c1 HAS NO STATUS LINE ON PURPOSE: tcsh abandons the whole command line when a redirection cannot be opened, so `echo c1=$status' never runs, and the refusal message is what the machine actually prints -- while `c1=0', which an unprotected machine WOULD print, is asserted absent.  THE cd ARM READS THE DIRECTORY AND NOT THE STATUS, because the status lies: tcsh answers 0 for a `cd' the kernel refused, while its own $cwd correctly stays put.  So the arm changes to /tmp, attempts /tmp/nx -- a directory the account OWNS and has chmod'd to 000, which denies the owner too since only root is exempt -- and prints $cwd each time.  A machine enforcing chdir(2)'s VEXEC never leaves /tmp; one that is not prints AT-/tmp/nx-AT, which is asserted absent.  The needle is built by expansion, so neither spelling appears in anything typed.  c5 RENAMES the account's own /tmp/mine OVER root's /etc/motd and must FAIL: a rename onto an existing name is a write to the TARGET's directory (Reno ufs/ufs_lookup.c:440, `flag == RENAME && wantparent'), and rename(2) walks the target with LOCKPARENT, which upstream's wantparent includes.
